_comment: Candidate freeze for GATE F RUN 3, the first run against the completed §H.1 evidence split. Written BEFORE segment 1 and not amended during the run: CD-8b's whole subject is a freeze record that claimed a capability the run did not have, and §H.1 is explicit that a run wanting a logic lane must say so here beforehand rather than editing this file to get a segment to start.
_comment_candidate: The GAME is frozen at main@26f0db4. This run changes no game code, data or config; see rig_sha.
_comment_rig: The rig commits on top of the candidate. They touch tools/gate_f/ only: the §H.1 split extended from S01 to every remaining segment, and one instrument fix. Recorded separately from candidate_sha so a reader is never left inferring whether a finding about the game came from a build edited to produce it.
_comment_discarded_attempt: An earlier attempt at this run (gate-f-run-20260828T182723Z) ran S01 only and was DISCARDED, not superseded, before any second segment. It found that `objective_is` compared the protocol's entry ids against the probe's flag ids and would have failed all 26 of those asserts across ten segments for a reason about the instrument. The fix is rig_sha's second commit. Nothing from that attempt is spliced into this run (§1.6); its directory is gone and its only finding is the one recorded here.

binary.kind: linux editor binary, NOT the shipped Windows export
binary._comment: §0.5. Byte-identical to the binary run 2 used, so the envelope measurements carried forward below are about the same executable.

logic._comment: §H.1's per-lane block, and the reason this run can start at all. A flat display_server field cannot describe a run that is headless for its logic and X11 for its capture, and a record with no `lanes` block binds EVERY segment by its flat claim -- which is why the 2026-08-27 candidate record blocks every logic segment run against it (verified: it does). --headless WITH a rendering driver hangs forever; --headless with none is correct and fast, and is what every segment of this run actually used.

capture.renderer: opengl3 / Compatibility under xvfb — llvmpipe software rasterisation
capture._comment: Declared, and NOT EXERCISED IN THIS RUN. No capture lane was run in this container and none should be. This entry says what the capture lanes need, not what happened.

_comment_resolution: The capture lanes' requested size. No capture smoke was run in this container because no capture lane was run.
input_mode: synthetic joypad + keyboard via Input.parse_input_event, paired with Input.action_press/release
operator: claude-opus-5 agent, Tetherbound lane session ralph/GATE-F-RUN-3
_comment_free_build: autoload/game_state.gd defaults free_build and debug_teleport to false and both persist only in user://settings.json, which the first wipe_saves clears. Teleport is off everywhere except the DIAG segments that turn it on deliberately (§0.6).
instrumentation_overhead_note: NOT re-measured in this container. Run 2's measurement stands as the last one taken (off 4.341, telemetry 3.945, telemetry+recording@0.50Hz 4.039 ms/frame, all deltas inside a 0.717 ms/frame noise floor, frames written 0 so the readback cost was never measured directly). It is also LESS load-bearing than it was: the recorder is off on every segment of this run by construction, because evidence_lane=logic forces record_hz to 0.

envelope_facts_confirmed_on_this_contain.why_no_capture_lane_ran: 12,721 ms per rendered frame against 6.1 ms of game logic under llvmpipe with no GPU. The eighteen segments ask for 4,607,802 physics frames; in capture mode that is ~8,283 hours. Measured in run 2 and carried forward rather than re-measured. It is a fact about the box, not about the game. The capture lanes are authored, checked and UNPAID: they need a GPU host.
envelope_facts_confirmed_on_this_contain.logic_frame_cost_measured_here: The logic lane's own price, measured by the pre-flight on this container: 0.0059 s/frame on the empty tree, 0.0065 s/frame re-priced on the title, 0.0166 s/frame in the standing Meadows. Higher than run 2's quoted 6.1 ms and still ~765x cheaper than a rendered frame.
envelope_facts_confirmed_on_this_contain.import_cache: Built from scratch on this container. 1,492 files under .godot/imported, identical across two consecutive passes, exit 0 both times, and zero SCRIPT ERROR / Parse Error / Failed to load / ERROR: Cannot open in either log.
envelope_facts_confirmed_on_this_contain.audio: Expected NONE (no ALSA card, no libpulse in this image). Any audio judgement is [OWNER-ONLY].

_comment_config_flags: §A.2 / CD-8, read mechanically from data/config/*.json rather than hand-listed. The one CD-8 was written about has CHANGED since run 2: grass_field.json:enabled is TRUE on this candidate, so the procedural ground cover is present and the boot log confirms it builds (315,232 tufts). It is absent from config_flags_off for that reason, not by omission. Nothing in config_flags_off is a finding by itself -- the vegetation collides/casts_shadow flags are settled art and performance decisions.

suite_state_at_freeze._comment: §A.4 makes a green suite a COORDINATOR precondition before the freeze, not an operator step, and §13 forbids substituting a unit-test result for player-path evidence. It was not re-run here: this container was provisioned bare. This field exists so a reader sees the actual state rather than an implied green.

owner_only_gaps: Unchanged from §K and asserted by NO evidence in this run: device frame rate, GPU frame time, VRAM, thermals/battery, real controller feel, 7-inch handheld legibility, first-time-human navigation/pacing, voluntary engagement, audio, Windows export identity, true continuous video, long-session device soak, mouse-look feel.

segments_planned._comment: Sixteen capture lanes owe 274 prescribed frames between them. None was run in this container. tools/gate_f/run_inventory.py reports that debt over this run directory at the end; a delegation nobody paid is a run-level deficiency and is meant to read as one.

clocks._comment: §H.2. Play time is Engine.get_physics_frames() over physics_ticks_per_second. In logic mode the two clocks run close together; the distinction still matters because §D's pacing numbers must be about the game.
